sub_graphs.title: EIP-1283: SSTORE Three-Value State Tracking
sub_graphs.description: Models the three-value tracking system for SSTORE gas metering (original, current, new)

nodes.label: SSTORE Opcode Invoked
nodes.description: EVM has encountered SSTORE opcode during execution

nodes.label: Get Original Value
nodes.description: Retrieve the storage slot value that would exist if the transaction reverted

nodes.label: Get Current Value
nodes.description: Retrieve the storage slot value before this SSTORE operation

nodes.label: Get New Value from Stack
nodes.description: Pop the new value to be stored from the stack

nodes.label: Three Values Loaded
nodes.description: Original, current, and new values are all known

nodes.label: Classify SSTORE Operation
nodes.description: Determine if operation is no-op, fresh, or dirty based on value comparisons

nodes.label: No-Op Classification
nodes.description: Current value equals new value - no actual change

nodes.label: Fresh Classification
nodes.description: Original equals current - slot unchanged in this transaction until now

nodes.label: Dirty Classification
nodes.description: Original differs from current - slot already modified in this transaction

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1283: SSTORE Gas Cost Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas cost calculation based on storage slot state transitions

nodes.label: No-Op Detected
nodes.description: SSTORE will not change the storage value

nodes.label: Charge 200 Gas (No-Op)
nodes.description: Deduct minimal gas for no-op SSTORE

nodes.label: Fresh State - Original Zero
nodes.description: Slot is fresh and originally zero (creating new storage)

nodes.label: Charge 20000 Gas (Create)
nodes.description: Deduct full gas for creating new storage entry

nodes.label: Fresh State - Original Non-Zero
nodes.description: Slot is fresh and originally had a value (modifying existing storage)

nodes.label: Charge 5000 Gas (Modify)
nodes.description: Deduct gas for modifying existing storage entry

nodes.label: Dirty State Detected
nodes.description: Slot has already been modified in this transaction

nodes.label: Charge 200 Gas (Dirty)
nodes.description: Deduct minimal gas for subsequent modifications

nodes.label: Gas Charged
nodes.description: SSTORE gas cost has been deducted

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1283: Gas Refund Mechanism
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas refund calculations for SSTORE operations

nodes.label: SSTORE Executed
nodes.description: SSTORE operation has been performed, refund calculation needed

nodes.label: Check Clear to Zero
nodes.description: Check if fresh slot is being set to zero (clearing storage)

nodes.label: Clearing Storage (Fresh)
nodes.description: Fresh non-zero slot being set to zero

nodes.label: Add 15000 to Refund Counter
nodes.description: Credit refund for clearing storage

nodes.label: Check Dirty Slot Clear
nodes.description: Check if dirty slot is being set to zero

nodes.label: Dirty Slot Cleared
nodes.description: Previously modified slot now being set to zero

nodes.label: Add 15000 Refund (Dirty Clear)
nodes.description: Credit refund for clearing dirty slot

nodes.label: Check Restore to Original
nodes.description: Check if dirty slot is being restored to original value

nodes.label: Restoring Original Value
nodes.description: Dirty slot being set back to original transaction value

nodes.label: Add Restore Refund
nodes.description: Credit 19800 (if original=0) or 4800 (if original!=0) refund

nodes.label: Check Undo Clear Operation
nodes.description: Check if previously cleared slot is being set to non-zero

nodes.label: Undoing Previous Clear
nodes.description: Slot that was cleared is now getting a value again

nodes.label: Remove 15000 from Refund Counter
nodes.description: Subtract from refund counter (clear bonus revoked)

nodes.label: Refund Calculated
nodes.description: All refund adjustments have been applied

sub_graphs.title: EIP-1283: Refund Counter Invariants
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation rules ensuring refund counter never goes negative at transaction level

nodes.label: Transaction Executing
nodes.description: Transaction is in progress, refund counter is accumulating

nodes.label: Refund Counter Non-Negative
nodes.description: Transaction-level refund counter is >= 0

nodes.label: Child Call Frame Entered
nodes.description: Execution has entered a sub-call with checkpointed refund

nodes.label: Frame Refund Counter Negative
nodes.description: Child frame's refund counter has gone negative (allowed)

nodes.label: Checkpoint Refund Counter
nodes.description: Save current refund counter before entering sub-call

nodes.label: Merge Frame Refund
nodes.description: Add child frame's refund delta to parent's refund counter

nodes.label: Transaction Complete
nodes.description: Transaction finished, final refund calculation

nodes.label: Apply Refund Cap
nodes.description: Cap refund at half of gas consumed

nodes.label: Refund Capped
nodes.description: Final refund limited to max(0, min(refund, gas_used/2))

ambiguities.text: The term 'original value' is defined as 'the value when the current transaction reverts' but does not explicitly state how this interacts with nested calls.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'original value' is the value at the start of the outermost transaction, not affected by any calls within the transaction.

ambiguities.text: The specification uses '~0' notation in state transition tables without defining it.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume '~0' means 'any non-zero value' and '~Original' means 'any value different from the original value'.

ambiguities.text: The interaction between EIP-1283 refund mechanism and the refund cap (50% of gas consumed) is mentioned but the exact application timing is unclear.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the refund cap is applied once at the end of transaction execution, after all SSTORE refunds have been accumulated.

implicit_assumptions.description: Client implementations can efficiently track the 'original value' for all storage slots accessed during a transaction without significant memory overhead.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Clients may run out of memory or slow down significantly when transactions access many unique storage slots.

implicit_assumptions.description: The refund mechanism cannot be exploited to profit from gas by creating artificial storage churn patterns.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could submit transactions that cost less gas than they receive in refunds, creating a gas printing attack vector.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing contracts were not designed with the assumption that multiple SSTOREs to the same slot would cost 20000 gas each.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts relying on high SSTORE gas costs for reentrancy protection could become vulnerable (this actually occurred, leading to the Constantinople delay).
